ai.title: Free tier agent exemption now requires specific model match
ai.summary: The free-tier small-request exemption for lightweight utility agents now requires both the agent ID and the specific model to match, replacing a simple agent-only check. This prevents arbitrary models from being charged zero credits when a lightweight helper like `file-picker` is running them. The change introduces `FREE_TIER_AGENT_MODELS` and `isFreeAgentModel` to enforce this model-level constraint, while updating documentation for daily session limits in the GPT-6.1 Sol promotion to clarify counting behavior.

eli5.text: The free-tier rule for small, automatic tasks (like quickly finding files) now checks both the task's name and the specific AI model doing the work. Previously, any model could perform these tiny tasks for free as long as the task had the right name; now, the model must also be on an approved list for that specific task. This change affects developers using the free tier who sometimes connect their own AI subscriptions; they will no longer see unexpected small charges when the assistant runs these quick helper tasks, provided the task uses an approved model. For most users, this is invisible maintenance that tightens billing accuracy; no action is needed, and existing sessions do not lose access.

In the `common` package, `matchesAllowedModel` in `free-agents.ts` narrows its regex from `^\d{6,8}(?:$|[-:])` to `^\d{6,8}$` to prevent bypassing the allowlist via variant features. The recognition helper `freebuffModelIdMatches` in `freebuff-models.ts` is explicitly documented as deliberately broader, ensuring that any id admitted by the allowlist is also recognized for caps and gates.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`, the regex in `matchesAllowedModel` is updated from `/^\d{6,8}(?:$|[-:])/.test(suffix)` to `/^\d{6,8}$/.test(suffix)`, and in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, the doc comment for `freebuffModelIdMatches` is updated to state it is 'Deliberately broader' than the allowlist and matches `[-:]` continuations.

eli5.text: The security check that decides which AI models a free user can use now blocks requests that add extra routing tags to a model name. Previously, a request could sneak past the free-tier limit by tacking on a specific provider tag to a date-stamped model name, but that shortcut is now closed. This change is internal and does not alter how free users access models, since they do not manually type these technical identifiers. The system still recognizes all valid model names for internal tracking and billing purposes, ensuring no accidental lockouts.

ai.summary: The base3 agent definition in the agents package removed system prompt instructions that told the model to produce minimal results early or reserve time for verification when a deadline is present. The agent runtime in packages/agent-runtime updated the completion check prompt to drop the phrase 'within the remaining budget' when instructing the model to finish missing checks. When a 400/422 names a replayed reasoning field as unsupported, the same request body without it — else undefined. Like `byokReasoningRetryBody`, the refusal is remembered for the connection revision.

A provider or model that refuses the picked reasoning effort, or replayed reasoning on assistant messages, still answers the task: once per field, without it, remembered for the connection so later steps do not send it again.
Error text that names the field we added, not merely any 400.
Undo `applyReasoningEffort`, or undefined when the body does not carry exactly what it would have added (e.g. direct Luna's own `'none'`).
